issues.legal_issue: A landlord with a direct legal interest in a building that may be demolished is a proper party to a tenant’s suit seeking to restrain the demolition, even when the tenant seeks no relief against the landlord.
material_facts: A lessee sued to restrain a municipal authority from demolishing part of a building after the authority issued a demolition notice alleging unauthorised construction.
The landlords sought to be added as parties, asserting a direct interest in the property.
Demolition would materially affect the landlords’ rights, title and interest in the property, regardless of whether the disputed construction had been made with their consent.
issues.conclusion: The landlords were proper parties to the suit, although no relief was sought against them, and the order adding them as parties was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a proper party is one whose presence is needed for complete and effectual adjudication, even if no relief is sought against that party. A necessary party is one without whom no effective and complete adjudication can be made and no relief granted. A direct or legal interest in the subject matter differs from a merely commercial interest. The Court distinguished Ramesh Hirachand Kundanmal v. Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay, where the notice concerned chattels in which the proposed party had no direct interest; it also referred to New Redbank Tea Co. Pvt. Ltd. v. Kumkum Mittal, Union of India v. District Judge, Udhampur, Bihar State Electricity Board v. State of Bihar, and Anil Kumar Singh v. Shivnath Mishra in applying the principles governing joinder of parties.

predicates.demolition_injunction_suit: A tenant brought a suit seeking to restrain a public authority from demolishing a building or part of it.
predicates.proposed_party_is_landlord: The person seeking to be joined is the landlord of the property involved in the suit.
predicates.demolition_would_materially_affect_landl: The proposed demolition would materially affect the landlord’s legal rights or interest in the property.

issues.definition: When a tenant sues to restrain demolition, and the proposed party is the landlord whose legal interest in the property would be materially affected by demolition, the landlord is a proper party.
